analysis: The PR changes only docs/provider/cli-reference.md: it bumps the 'Last updated' date (line 3) and extends the GLM video-input sentence at line 52 to say constant or variable frame rate inline data:video/mp4 or quicktime input is sampled at 2 FPS and decoded target-only. No code, configuration, authorization, attestation, encryption or protocol behavior changes in this diff. I read the rest of the supplied document (lines 1-821) for contradictions with the threat model. The logout, device-revoke, drain, cache-storage and Autopilot text is consistent with the A-008, T-041 and TB-011 descriptions: it does not claim remote revocation without HTTP 204, it keeps cache scope unchanged, and it says Autopilot shadow mode grants no authority. The documented video decode path touches T-050 (inline video plaintext exposed through temp files). The doc line only describes variable-frame-rate support; the video-handling implementation that would show whether the new VFR path writes plaintext to temp files is not in the supplied evidence. If the paired code change adds VFR decoding, a later pass should confirm it keeps the T-050 no-plaintext-temp-file mitigation and bounds frame-count/duration for resource use (TB-007, T-010). This is an unverified contract, not a finding. No threat-model update is needed from this documentation-only change.
